interpretation: R2487 explicitly calls quoted operator RHS notation metadata, not an executed CFEL expression; quoted operator spelling alone does not define general string lexing.
R2720 contains a double-quoted outer metadata literal with backslash-escaped inner quotes as used syntax; it does not establish a complete CFEL escape table.

R1931 says backslash escapes the next literal name character and quotes are carrier serialization, not Entity-name delimiters. That applies to Entity paths and conflicts with treating embedded Subject quote marks as general Entity delimiters; R2637 shows a quoted multiword value in a selector, requiring reconciliation rather than assuming universal Subject quote semantics.
R2462 and R2707 show bare multiword values; p: [int] and existing [int, 1+] appear in Current; user-approved [int,0..100] is a new decision, not claimed as Current authority.
Current R2598 still declares fallback ?=; user-specified ?== is a pending new default-assignment decision, not Current quoted token.
minimal_proposal: Keep existing readable bare multiword names/values where context and declared domain make them unambiguous; allow double-quoted literal text where punctuation would otherwise be parsed as CFEL syntax, following already-observed operator metadata style. Preserve Entity-path escaping as a separate rule. Define the actual quote/backslash and other escape handling explicitly before adoption; do not infer a JSON escape set. Distinguish quoted literal values from declared model references by operand context and authority; do not turn literal text into a Node.
one_question: For CFEL literal values containing syntax characters, should we use double quotes while leaving unambiguous multiword values bare—for example, retain `Label == Scope Contract`, but write `Label == "A/B"` when the slash is text—and how should an actual double quote or backslash inside that literal be written?
blast_radius: Affects literal tokenization in Formal Claims, quoted selector values, operator descriptors and relation-alias metadata; existing Subject path escapes are a separate compatibility check. Existing unquoted model references and named numeric format ranges need not be renamed.
